During his tenure as Apple's CEO, one of Tim Cook's most delicate tasks has been walking the tightrope between defending the company's values and avoiding antagonising the White House on issues ranging from immigration policy to diversity and inclusion.

After transitioning to the newly created role of executive chairman, he retains government liaison duties, providing a degree of protection for his successor as CEO, John Ternus……

Past challenges

The challenges Cook has faced in the past stretch back years. In 2018, for example, changes to US immigration policy and practices affected thousands of Apple employees. Cook joined fellow CEOs in writing to the government at the time, saying the changes left "many Apple employees feeling deep concern" and were "threatening to interfere with company operations."

Last year, Cook faced a similar predicament when Trump demanded Apple abandon its diversity and inclusion policies. In response, Cook said the company would comply with any legal changes but would not abandon its values.

Cook is now Apple's official diplomat

Apple has confirmed that Cook's new responsibilities include liaising with governments around the world.

Attending a White House dinner next week

Bloomberg reports that Cook will attend a White House state dinner for the Chinese president next week. US-China relations are currently at a tense moment, particularly when it comes to artificial intelligence.

9to5Mac's Take

I'm willing to bet big that the idea of Cook taking on the diplomatic role was his own. It's a self-sacrificing move designed to shield his successor from unnecessary distractions and controversies.

Ternus will, of course, still be limited in what he can say in response to controversial policies and laws, whether in the US, China or elsewhere. But handing off the responsibility for official responses to someone else does give him considerably more wiggle room.
